blocks.text: Carboxylic acids are considerably more acidic than phenols, and phenols are more acidic than alcohols. The strength of an acid, the extent to which it ionises, depends on the stability of its conjugate base. For ethanoic acid, CH3COOH <=> CH3COO- + H+, Ka = 1.8 x 10^-5 and pKa = 4.76.

blocks.title: pKa
blocks.text: pKa = -log Ka. The higher the Ka, or the lower the pKa, the stronger the acid.

In the ethanoate ion the negative charge is not held on one oxygen: the electrons are delocalised over the -COO- group, so the charge is shared by both oxygens. This stabilises the ethanoate ion and makes it less likely to accept an H+ ion and re-form the undissociated acid.

Substituents change the acidity. An electron-donating group (+I effect) destabilises the carboxylate ion by intensifying its negative charge, and so weakens the acid. An electron-withdrawing group (-I effect) stabilises the carboxylate ion by spreading its negative charge, and so strengthens the acid. Methanoic acid (Ka = 1.8 x 10^-4, pKa 3.75) is ten times stronger than ethanoic acid (Ka = 1.8 x 10^-5, pKa 4.75), because the methyl group of ethanoic acid is electron-donating. Chlorine atoms are strongly electron-withdrawing, so each extra chlorine makes the acid stronger.

blocks.alt: Top: the two equivalent structures of the ethanoate ion, with the negative charge on one oxygen or the other, joined by a double-headed arrow. Bottom left: the book's Ka and pKa values, RCOOH 10^-5 (5), ArOH 10^-10 (10), HOH 10^-14 (14), ROH 10^-16 (16). Bottom right: bars for the pKa values of ethanoic (4.74), chloroethanoic (2.86), dichloroethanoic (1.26) and trichloroethanoic acid (0.64).
blocks.caption: Delocalisation in the ethanoate ion and the relative acidities (original diagram after the book's structures and Table 23.1).
blocks.long_description: The ethanoate ion is a single structure between the two drawn, with the charge shared equally by both oxygens. Carboxylic acids have the lowest pKa of the four classes. Each chlorine atom pulls electron density away from the COO- group, stabilising it further, so the pKa falls as more chlorine atoms are added.

items: Methanoic acid is stronger than ethanoic acid. Give the reason.
Place CH3CH2COOH, CH3CCl2COOH and CH3CHClCOOH in order of strength, strongest first.
Explain why ethanoic acid is a stronger acid than ethanol.
